predecessors.note: The Imamate was "founded by Imam Omar who successfully rebelled against and defeated the Ajuran Sultanate"; the Darandoolle, a section of the Hiraab, first challenged the Ajuran, and other clans later drove them out of Galguduud and Mudug (no year).

successors.note: Infobox disestablishment 7 January 1889, the date of the first Somali-Italian treaty of friendship and commerce; "Imam Mahmud Imam Binyamin of the Mogadishu faction signed a protectorate treaty" (undated); Benadir became Southern Italian Somaliland in 1910.

correction.text: "the Shabelle valley, Galguduud, Mudug, and the coast toward Hobyo"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. "By 1700, the Hiraab and other clans occupied a large territory", the Shabelle valley, Galguduud, Mudug and the coast toward Hobyo; "By 1870, the Imamate had declined internally", which led to decentralization. No area on the page. The Banaadir and the lower Shabelle overlap the Geledi Sultanate (geledi-sultanate), whose capital Afgooye lay near Mogadishu.

ledger.note: Late 17th century: Imam Omar founds the Hiraab Imamate at Mogadishu. Infobox "Late 17th century"; "founded by Imam Omar who successfully rebelled against and defeated the Ajuran Sultanate". The page gives no year: 1690 is a placeholder.

By 1700: the Hiraab hold Galguduud, Mudug and the Shabelle valley. "By 1700, the Hiraab and other clans occupied a large territory"; the Habar Gidir and Duduble "later drove them out of Galguduud and Mudug" (no year).

ledger.note: 7 January 1889: the Imamate ends at the first Somali-Italian treaty. Infobox disestablishment date 7 January 1889: "Sultan Abiker signed the first Somali-Italian treaty of friendship and commerce on 7 January 1889". The text goes on to Italian actions until the 1920s (1890 ambush at Warsheikh, 1908 and 1910 reorganisations).

wars.name: French incursion at Mogadishu
wars.outcome: The Imamate repelled a French incursion at Mogadishu in 1701; in 1707 a British naval boat sent ashore was detained.

wars.name: Omani bombardment of Mogadishu
wars.outcome: Oman bombed Mogadishu's port in 1828 (described as British-sponsored); no land changed hands.
wars.note: The page does not say Oman occupied the town.

notes: New dossier: Cliopatria lacks the Hiraab Imamate. Pages opened: Hiraab Imamate, Ajuran Sultanate (2). The page gives no founding year (infobox 'Late 17th century'), so start 1690 and the 1700 expansion are weak placeholders; the Ajuran page gives 1695 for the end of the Ajuran. Two ruler tables on the page conflict (Imam Cumar I 1600-1646 ... Imam Caamir II 1870-1928 against Imam Mohamed II 1808-1841 ... Imam Mohamud III 1866-1907), so no ruler strip. The infobox ends the Imamate on 7 January 1889 though the page runs Imams to 2021 and the Benadir protectorate to 1908-1910; the 1889 date is kept. Overlap: the Banaadir and the middle Shabelle with the Geledi Sultanate (geledi-sultanate dossier uses Shabeellaha Hoose and Banaadir). Counterpart strings 'France' and 'sultanate-of-oman' are not dossiers of this batch.
